newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude values steady, paper quiet.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude values steady, paper quiet.

text.p: North Sea physical crude differentials were steady in meagre business on Thursday despite an OPEC-related slide in outright values, traders said.
Front month August IPE Brent crude futures were trading down 35 cents at $17.87 a barrel, hit by mounting scepticism about OPEC's ability to stick to renewed pledges of quota adherence.
The contract had jumped 35 cents on Wednesday after OPEC announced a "firm" commitment to respect output ceilings.
"It's hard to take this seriously," said a trader. "In two days everyone will have forgotten about OPEC and the members will go back to their countries and continue overproducing."
Traders pointed to a denial by suspected quota-buster Venezuela that it had admitted overproducing -- a move traders said would have been the first step to grapple with real issues.
Paper was quiet. Most traders avoiding business for fear of being wrong-footed by OPEC-inspired futures price gyrations.
Traders said a Brent loading July 8-10 moved from a trader to a major equity holder on Wednesday at August Brent -25 cents but this could not be confirmed by the parties.
An Ekofisk loading around July 16 changed hands at a 20 cent premium to international benchamrk Dated Brent, unchanged from a trade on Wednesday.
A 500,000 barrel Oseberg loading July 9-11 moved at 12 cents above Dated, three cents weaker than another Oseberg traded on Thursday in an exchange for a Statfjord.
The Oseberg loading July 22-24 was swapped at dated +15 cents for a Statfjord loading July 21-23 at Dated +34 cents.
The status of the single wet Brent turning wet on Thursday appeared in dispute between Cargill and Esso, traders said.
Indian Oil Corp (IOC) awarded four cargoes of Dubai, possibly two of Qua Iboe and one each of Gulf of Suez and Escravos in its August crude buying tender, traders said.
